description:
File: crate-jmap-chat-server/src/memory.rs (11 test-only methods)

The reference MemoryBackend exposes 11 test-helper methods. The
stability signaling across these 11 methods is inconsistent on
three orthogonal axes — even though all 11 serve the same role
(test-only entry points that production callers must not use):

Axis 1: #[doc(hidden)]
  Present on 9 of 11:
    set_retains_edit_history_for_test           (line 251)
    set_protect_last_admin_for_test             (line 270)
    apply_space_patch_with_caller_id            (line 299)
    apply_space_metadata_patch_with_caller_id   (line 330)
    set_limits_for_test                         (line 352)
    insert_object_for_test                      (line 367)
    first_category_id                           (line 386)
    peek_chat                                   (line 416)
    (plus 2 'normal' constructors: new, register_account)
  Missing on 2 of 11:
    new                                         (line 169)
    register_account                            (line 175)

Axis 2: `_for_test` name suffix
  Present on 5 of 9 hidden methods:
    set_retains_edit_history_for_test
    set_protect_last_admin_for_test
    set_limits_for_test
    insert_object_for_test
    (one more)
  Missing on 4 of 9 hidden methods:
    apply_space_patch_with_caller_id
    apply_space_metadata_patch_with_caller_id
    first_category_id
    peek_chat

Axis 3: verbatim 'Production callers must not use this method'
banner sentence in the doc-comment
  Present on 5 of 9 hidden methods:
    set_protect_last_admin_for_test
    apply_space_patch_with_caller_id
    apply_space_metadata_patch_with_caller_id
    set_limits_for_test
    insert_object_for_test
  Missing on 4 of 9 hidden methods:
    set_retains_edit_history_for_test  (says 'default false matching
                                         trait default' but no banner)
    first_category_id                  (says 'Test-only' + Panics)
    peek_chat                          (says 'Test-only' + Panics)
    (and the 2 non-hidden: new, register_account)

A reader trying to decide 'can I call this from production?' has
to apply three independent mental tests with three different
answer-distributions. A 'contributor writing a new test method'
has no canonical pattern to follow.

Engineering basis (not stylistic):

1. The pattern is the documented intent — see the explicit
   'Production callers must not use this method' banner on the
   5 methods that have it. The other 4 deviate from the explicit
   intent of the pattern.

2. Once the inconsistency ships, a future cleanup pass that
   normalizes all 11 to follow the same pattern becomes a
   breaking change for the 4 deviating methods (renaming
   first_category_id → first_category_id_for_test is breaking).

3. New contributors will copy the nearest existing pattern. The
   inconsistency makes 'nearest' ambiguous and reproduces the
   defect.

Recommended fix: write down the pattern as a comment / banner at
the top of the test-helper section in memory.rs, then mechanically
align all 11 methods to it. Suggested canonical:

  - All test methods: #[doc(hidden)] + `_for_test` suffix +
    verbatim banner.
  - Public stable methods: no hidden, no suffix, no banner —
    only `new` qualifies; `register_account` should NOT
    qualify (see JMAP-x2gd.48).

Sibling: JMAP-x2gd.48 (register_account specific case).
title: API contract: MemoryBackend test-helper stability signaling is inconsistent on three orthogonal axes
